transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-23 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52m
Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Archipelago Head of Partnerships), Sana Roy (Cloud Architect), Mateo Alvarez (Procurement), Priya Kapoor (Security), Ethan Park (Platform)

Summary:
Quick partner intro to explore integration for Archipelago's brokerage layer — they broker GPU capacity across regional clouds and want faster routing + unified API. Focus areas: routing policies, private deployments (VPC peering / on-prem), pricing tradeoffs, and a short pilot to validate latency/throughput and cost.

[00:00] Jordan: all right hey everyone thanks for making time, um I'm Jordan from Redwood AE, this is Maya our solutions engineer. we're excited to talk about Archipelago's "cloudbridge" broker idea.
[00:18] Liam: yeah thanks for having us, quick intro — i'm Liam, i run partnerships, we've been building a multi-cloud broker for gpu orchestration, basically customers want single API and we route to a mix of partners.
[00:31] Maya: cool, nice to meet you all. can you give us a little more context on what a successful integration looks like? like is this about routing to Redwood hosted endpoints, dedicated pools, or on-prem connectors?
[00:45] Sana: short answer: all of the above. the broker needs to be able to route depending on cost/latency/region. for regulated clients we need VPC-backed private deployments. for some startup customers we might route to hosted endpoints.
[01:02] Jordan: ok good, good. so we support Hosted API, Dedicated reserved pools, and Private (VPC/on-prem) — that's pretty aligned. maybe to set expectations, the tradeoffs you'll see are predictable throughput and isolation on Dedicated/Private vs the fastest onboarding on Hosted.
[01:18] Mateo: procurement question up front — will there be a reseller arrangement or is this going to be a channel rev-share? we don't have procurement terms ironed out yet.
[01:27] Jordan: fair. we'll surface both options in the checklist. for initial pilots it's usually a usage arrangement then expand to commit pricing or channel agreement.
[01:36] Priya: on security: SOC2 type II, audit logs, KMS/HSM integration, and SSO via SAML are must-haves. we also need tenant separation assurances.
[01:46] Maya: understood. Redwood supports KMS integrations and SAML SSO, and we can produce audit logs per request. we'll drop our security whitepaper link — though note sometimes the auto transcript will call it something else — but yes we'll share docs.
[02:00] Ethan: technical q — how would the routing handshake work? do you expect a prefix key cache, or do we call an endpoint per request?
[02:08] Maya: good q. typical pattern: Archipelago would call Redwood's routing API with metadata (tenant, latency target, cost priority). Redwood's smart router picks model variant and deployment (hosted vs dedicated). for latency-sensitive, we can route to warmed dedicated capacity and maintain prefetched KV cache to cut warmup.
[02:25] Liam: warmed dedicated meaning you'd keep models resident on the gpu? that's important for our low-latency customers.
[02:31] Maya: yes, resident KV cache + persistent model memory on dedicated nodes. we also do continuous batching and automatic prefix caching where it makes sense. sometimes we see the transcript miss 'KV cache' as 'kev cass', so apologies if this export gets funky.
[02:46] Sana: our main flinch is around network topology — our broker sits in customer's VPC and we want Redwood's private control plane to be able to talk back without permitting wide egress. can you do VPC peering or a connector appliance?
[03:00] Jordan: we have a couple of options — VPC peering in cloud regions, private link-like connectors, or on-prem package for air-gapped customers. peering requires some setup but gives you network-level isolation.
[03:13] Priya: and how do you handle customer data at rest and in transit? encryption, customer-managed keys?
[03:20] Maya: data in flight is TLS. at rest we support customer-managed keys with common KMS providers; for Private deployments we can integrate with HSM if needed. we'll include specifics in the security pack.
[03:35] Mateo: pricing — for the broker flow where we route a bunch of small requests, cost per token matters a lot, but also for customers that need strict latency the dedicated route is more expensive. can you provide guidance on when to choose which?
[03:48] Jordan: yes. high-level guidance: Hosted is lowest setup friction; cost per-token is competitive for bursty low-SLA workloads. Dedicated gives predictable throughput and lower p99 for high-volume low-latency workloads but it requires monthly commit. Optimize (our tooling) can suggest batching and quantization profiles to cut unit cost by 20–40% depending on workload.
[04:10] Ethan: do you support different quantization levels per model variant so we can trade quality vs cost at runtime?
[04:16] Maya: yep — we have model variants and quantization profiles, and the router can pick a variant based on labels you pass. some subtlety: highly quantized models can affect certain evals, so our Optimize tooling hooks into evals to guard quality regressions.
[04:32] Liam: curious — any partner-specific routing SDKs or do we just call the REST endpoints?
[04:37] Maya: REST + SDKs. for partner integrations we usually provide a small SDK that helps with auth, error handling, and backoff, but the core is simple HTTP/JSON.
[04:46] (crosstalk)
[04:50] Speaker 7: i'm hearing knock-on effects for metrics — can you emit per-request tokens and latency with tags so we can bill customers?
[04:59] Jordan: yes we emit token-level cost, latency breakdowns, and route tags. Redwood Console has per-route dashboards and you can pull via API.
[05:10] Sana: demo ask — would be useful to get a short demo of routing decisions and a dashboard showing fallbacks when a region is constrained.
[05:18] Jordan: happy to run that in the next session. SE-led demo focusing on routing, failover, and the console.
[05:23] Mateo: procurement constraint — we'll likely need a trial PO and a statement of work that lists SLA and support response times.
[05:31] Jordan: we can do a pilot SOW that lists target p50/p95, support windows, and escalation paths.
[05:36] Priya: one sticky point: some of our regulated customers require raw request retention to be zeroed by the vendor; can Redwood support configurable retention windows or no-retention modes?
[05:47] Maya: yes, retention windows are configurable; we have a strict no-storage mode for certain Private deployments. we'll confirm details for the pilot.
[05:58] Sana: on the connectivity side, do you support mutual TLS or client certs for API calls from our broker?
[06:05] Maya: mutual TLS is supported on Private endpoints. for Hosted we do token-based auth; for higher assurance we can do private links with mTLS.
[06:15] Liam: client success question — what's the expected timeline to go from pilot to production?
[06:21] Jordan: typical is 6–12 weeks: pilot (2–4 weeks) to validate latency/cost, then integration and SOC2/security review (2–6 weeks), then scale. depends on paperwork and infra changes.
[06:33] Ethan: benchmarks — can Redwood run a quick p95 and throughput test for our typical request mix? we can provide traffic replay.
[06:40] Maya: yes, we can run bench with traffic replay, but note for dedicated we may request capacity reservation. we'll supply a bench script and sample metrics sheet.
[06:50] Liam: on competitor note, we've seen NimbusCloud's routing offering but their observability was weak; if Redwood can show strong cost breakdown per token that's a differentiator.
[06:59] Jordan: yep that's a place we lean into. our Console has token-level cost and model variant breakdowns.
[07:06] (longer discussion on deployment variants and example pilot)
[12:20] Maya: quick architecture sketch — your broker calls /route with meta: tenant_id, priority (latency/cost), model_hint, seq_len_est. Redwood returns endpoint, model_variant, and warmup_token_count. you then stream user input to that endpoint.
[12:40] Sana: ack, that should map cleanly. one more network question — we may prefer a hop-less path for low-latency flows; do you support co-locating an inference boundary in our VPC?
[12:50] Maya: yes, Private deployment can place the serving runtime in your VPC or on-prem, gives hop-less. it does require more ops but gives best p95.
[13:10] Mateo: on pricing sheet, can you show both channel and reseller pricing variants? we need to see what margins we have as a broker.
[13:18] Jordan: we'll include reseller pricing and a sample rev-share tiering.
[13:22] Priya: about audit logs — do you provide immutable logs and integration with SIEMs?
[13:28] Maya: yes, audit logs can be exported to your SIEM via secure delivery; we can sign and timestamp logs for compliance.
[13:35] (discussion about fallback policies)
[18:05] Maya: FYI we have automatic fallback policies — if a selected model variant or region hits capacity we can route to a compatible fallback variant or to a lower-cost region subject to policy. that helps keep customers online.
[18:18] Liam: perfect that's one of the main values — graceful degradation is key.
[18:25] Sana: any gotchas with quantized models and function calling? some of our customers use heavy tool calling flows.
[18:33] Maya: some function-calling semantics can be impacted by strong quantization; we recommend evaluating the top prompts in the Optimize eval suite. we'll include a sample eval harness.
[18:46] Ethan: onboarding ops — how much infra automation do you provide for Private installs? ansible/terraform?
[18:53] Jordan: we have Terraform modules and an on-prem installer; for Private we do an onboarding runbook and partner runbook for a hands-on setup.
[19:04] (note from Jordan linking docs)
[19:10] Jordan: i'll post the partner integration checklist, the security pack link, and a short pricing matrix. Link to checklist: https://redwood.example/partners/checklist (will send in follow up)
[19:20] Liam: that will be helpful.
[19:24] (customer asks about long-term SLA numbers)
[19:30] Maya: typical committed-latency SLAs are in Dedicated contracts — we can provide p99/p95 targets in SOW. Hosted is best-effort but still low latency.
[19:40] Mateo: procurement asks: sample contract, indemnification and data handling terms — we will need redlines.
[19:46] Jordan: we'll share a sample MSP/reseller contract and propose an initial pilot SOW.
[19:52] (wrap-up begins)
[43:00] Jordan: to recap — action items: we'll send checklist/SOW draft, Maya will prepare KV/cache+quantization notes, Archipelago to share traffic profile, Priya to send security reqs. we propose a SE demo on routing and console next week, and a pilot planning session the following week.
[43:28] Liam: sounds good, thanks everyone. excited to run the pilot.
[43:34] Sana: thanks all, talk soon.
[43:38] Jordan: thanks, bye.

Notes/Artifacts referenced:
- Partner integration checklist (link to be sent)
- Security pack + SOC2 evidence (redwood security whitepaper)
